_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4469 / req 2d072437-c19d-49a4-ae89-f20b6185571f — AtomicFrontmatterService, the `claim`/`spawn` write channel. MA1 restores the local LF/CRLF-only regex this service carried until #4469 and therefore reddens BOTH the widenings (lone-CR, BOM) and the two DELIBERATE narrowings (a trailing-whitespace opening fence is no longer a block; blank lines after the closing fence survive) — that a single mutant covers all four is the point: they are one change of predicate, not four. MA2 and MA3 split the two properties that are NOT the predicate (the BOM survives as exactly one byte; only ONE line ending is consumed after the closing fence). Expectations written BEFORE the run.

MA1_back_to_the_local_lf_crlf_regex._note: The predicate this service carried until #4469. CH22 (the verify handshake) is listed because it REDDENS, not because its statement is about the predicate: it drives the same lone-CR fixture, so the predicate decides whether its call reaches the verify step at all. Measured, then written down — the first edition of this spec omitted it and the driver refused the run (integration-test-revert-verify §A44: an expectation derived from the mutant's THEME rather than from which axes execute). CH23 (LF/CRLF control) and CH26 (no fence) stay green, which is what makes the mutant pointed rather than broad.

MA2_bom_dropped_on_write._note: The channel would still RECOGNISE a BOM-prefixed asset and then silently re-encode it without the mark. Only the BOM axis reddens — recognition and preservation are two guarantees.

MA3_body_lead_swallows_every_blank_line._note: Restores the greedy `---\s*` behaviour of the old regex, which ate every blank line between the closing fence and the first body text. Nothing else moves.
